title: n8n deletes its execution history after fourteen days by default
content:
The shipped defaults are `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE=true`, `EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE=336` hours and `EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE_MAX_COUNT=10000`. The documentation confirms the behaviour rather than merely permitting it: *"n8n enables pruning by default"*, removing *"finished executions along with their execution data and binary data"* when either the age or the count threshold trips.

Being fair to n8n, it does save successful runs — `EXECUTIONS_DATA_SAVE_ON_SUCCESS` defaults to `all`. The gap is not that it never records. It is that it records and then deletes on a timer, 336 hours being fourteen days.

That is a defensible design for an orchestrator whose execution log is a debugging aid. It is disqualifying for anything expected to answer a question a year later.
description: EXECUTIONS_DATA_PRUNE ships true with EXECUTIONS_DATA_MAX_AGE at 336 hours, so the free edition forgets by design rather than by misconfiguration.
